They derive exact relations to the Sérsic R^{1/n} family (R_5 = (2n/b_n)^n R_e, with limit e^{1/6} as n→∞), reparameterize the model in terms of observable pair (R_5, μ_5), provide an exact single-integral identity relating projected to intrinsic light fractions, and construct the n-dependent Wolf-type mass estimator M_-3 using the anisotropy-insensitive intrinsic radius r_-3.
AI.result: The R_5 scale removes non-linear coupling between radial scale and Sérsic index n, cancels correlated measurement errors in radius and surface brightness when deriving total magnitudes, and eliminates systematic concentration-dependent offsets of 12-18% in enclosed mass and >20% in mass-to-light ratios present in half-light-based estimators. Dynamical mass estimators for dark-matter-free stellar systems are also provided.
AI.conclusion: The gradient-defined scale R_5 provides a physically motivated, less arbitrary alternative to the half-light radius that improves both photometric parameterization and dynamical mass estimation for stellar systems.

title: The Stellar Population of NGC 346 in the Small Magellanic Cloud with JWST
comment: Paper accepted to The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, 34 pages, 13 figures
summary: NGC 346 is a massive star-forming region located at a distance of $\sim$62 kpc, in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Due to its low metallicity (Z $\sim$1/5 Z$_{\odot}$), it is an ideal environment to study star formation and stellar population analogues to those at Cosmic Noon. In this work, we produce a combined JWST NIRCam and MIRI photometric catalogue of NGC 346. We characterise different stellar populations in the region: the upper main sequence (UMS), red giant branch (RGB), and red clump (RC), as well as pre-main sequence (pre-MS) stars and young stellar objects (YSOs). We performed point-spread function (PSF) weighted photometry in 11 wavelength bands across NIRCam and MIRI and utilised multiple colour-magnitude-diagrams to identify the various stellar populations in the field. Our final photometric catalogue of NGC 346 comprises 249,519 unique sources, including 2,024 UMS stars, 2,755 RGB stars and 742 RC stars. In addition, we identified 6,274 candidate pre-MS stars, 7,350 candidate YSOs and 23,819 IR-excess sources. Combining these three categories, we characterised 1,583 strong and 3,761 likely pre-MS/YSO candidates. By utilising the F115W-F200W vs F115W-F187N colour-colour diagram, we found 239 non-spurious sources with Pa$α$ excess, indicating accretion and star formation in NGC 346. Using JWST NIRCam and MIRI observations, we produced the deepest catalogue to date of the star formation region NGC 346 in the near- and mid-IR range (1-21$~μ$m). Our catalogue and characterisations of the young and old populations will provide the basis for detailed follow-up studies.

AI.tldr: This paper produces the deepest JWST NIRCam and MIRI photometric catalogue to date of NGC 346, a massive low-metallicity star-forming region in the SMC. The catalogue contains 249,519 unique sources across 11 wavelength bands (1-21 μm), with ~2,024 upper main sequence stars, 2,755 RGB stars, 742 RC stars, 6,274 pre-main sequence candidates, 7,350 YSO candidates, 23,819 IR-excess sources, and 239 sources showing Paα excess indicative of accretion.
AI.motivation: NGC 346 is a massive star-forming region in the Small Magellanic Cloud with low metallicity (Z ~1/5 Z_sun), making it an ideal local analogue for studying star formation and stellar populations similar to those found at Cosmic Noon (high redshift). A deep multi-wavelength photometric catalogue is needed to characterize both evolved and young stellar populations in this environment.
AI.method: The authors combine JWST NIRCam and MIRI imaging into a single photometric survey. They perform point-spread function (PSF)-weighted photometry in 11 wavelength bands across both instruments and construct multiple colour-magnitude diagrams to classify and characterise distinct stellar populations including UMS, RGB, RC, pre-MS stars, and YSOs. Colour-colour diagrams (e.g., F115W-F200W vs F115W-F187N) are used to identify Paα excess sources indicating ongoing accretion.
AI.result: The final catalogue comprises 249,519 unique sources: 2,024 UMS, 2,755 RGB, and 742 RC stars. They identified 6,274 candidate pre-MS stars, 7,350 candidate YSOs, and 23,819 IR-excess sources, with 1,583 strong and 3,761 likely pre-MS/YSO candidates. The colour-colour analysis yielded 239 non-spurious Paα excess sources, tracing active accretion and star formation.
AI.conclusion: This represents the deepest near- and mid-infrared (1-21 μm) catalogue of NGC 346 to date. The catalogue and population characterisations of both young and old stellar populations provide a robust foundation for detailed follow-up studies of star formation in low-metallicity environments, relevant to understanding star formation at Cosmic Noon.

title: Concerns regarding recurrent fluorescence's impact on smaller diffuse ISM aromatics
comment: To appear in publication
summary: Recent research implied that recurrent fluorescence (RF) could bolster smaller aromatics against fragmentation in the diffuse ISM, yet that hypothesis is contested by timescales for unrelenting dissociative recombination (electrons), and unceasing dissociating photons. Specifically, neutral cyanonaphthalene can sustain $13.6$ eV photoionization, and the ensuing cation's excess energy is channeled through intramolecular vibrational redistribution (IVR), with RF providing the radiative stabilization pathway ($\simeq7$ eV negligible survival limit). However, that cation endures dissociative recombination every $τ\approx0.5^{+5.6}_{-0.4}$ years, which deposits $\simeq 8.6$ eV and exceeds the limit. Moreover, that is paired with $7-13.6$ eV photodestruction each $τ\approx16^{+223}_{-14}$ years (total visual dust extinction $A_V=0-1$, and $τ\approx4^{+7}_{-2}$ years for $A_V\approx0$). Recent laboratory characterizations of RF were seminal, but the mechanism may not overturn models indicating a gap in smaller $N_C\approx7-11$ diffuse ISM aromatics, nor support those molecules as viable diffuse interstellar band carriers.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether recurrent fluorescence (RF) can protect small aromatic molecules from destruction in the diffuse interstellar medium (ISM), concluding that while RF is a real radiative stabilization mechanism, it cannot overcome the dominant destruction channels—dissociative recombination with electrons and direct photodissociation—thus leaving a gap in small carbon-number aromatics (N_C≈7–11) and questioning their viability as diffuse interstellar band (DIB) carriers.
AI.motivation: Recent work suggested that recurrent fluorescence (RF) might stabilize small aromatics against fragmentation in the diffuse ISM, potentially explaining their survival and role as diffuse interstellar band (DIB) carriers. However, this hypothesis is contested by considerations of competing destruction mechanisms, namely dissociative recombination with electrons and sustained photon-driven dissociation.
AI.method: The authors analyze the survival prospects of specific aromatic cations (notably cyanonaphthalene) in the diffuse ISM by quantitatively comparing the radiative stabilization pathway (RF, with a ~7 eV excess energy survival limit) against destruction channels, including dissociative recombination (dissociative recombination, which deposits ~8.6 eV, every τ≈0.5 years) and photodestruction by 7–13.6 eV photons (every τ≈16 years for A_V=0–1, or τ≈4 years for A_V≈0). They also incorporate recent laboratory characterizations of RF.
AI.result: The analysis shows that the cation undergoes dissociative recombination every ~0.5 years, depositing ~8.6 eV—exceeding the ~7 eV RF survival limit—and additionally faces photodestruction on timescales of 4–16 years. These destruction rates are far faster than any protective effect RF might confer, indicating that RF cannot overturn existing models that predict a deficit of small aromatics (N_C≈7–11) in the diffuse ISM.
AI.conclusion: Although recent laboratory measurements of recurrent fluorescence are seminal contributions, the RF mechanism is insufficient to enable small aromatics to survive in the diffuse ISM. They therefore cannot be supported as viable diffuse interstellar band carriers, and the previously identified gap in the population of smaller aromatics remains.

title: The segmented spiral structure of the Solar neighbourhood traced by young clustered populations
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The Milky Way spiral pattern remains poorly constrained, and the youngest tracers in the solar neighbourhood do not always follow a few smooth, continuous logarithmic arms. We analyse young open clusters, both independently and combined with young stellar object (YSO)-based groups, to test whether they define continuous spiral-arm ridges or shorter, partially connected structures. In the (theta_G, ln R_G) plane, we identify local overdensities using a density-supported Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (BGMM), introducing published Perseus, Local, Sagittarius, and Scutum arm tracks only afterwards as reference curves. We then apply a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) analysis in the heliocentric (X,Y) plane to examine spatial connectivity. The open-cluster sample already resolves into several local components, while the addition of YSO-based groups highlights branches and intermediate regions without producing continuous arms. The MST likewise shows distinct local branches at small pruning scales that progressively merge as the linking scale increases. The Local--Sagittarius region provides the clearest agreement between both diagnostics: the BGMM identifies an intermediate component between the reference arms, while the MST connects neighbouring branches through the same region. Overall, young structures near the Sun appear as fragmented, spiral-like segments with partial links rather than smooth continuations of a few grand-design arms. Determining whether this morphology reflects spiral-arm formation mechanisms or subsequent evolution will require additional age, vertical, and kinematic information.

title: The Spin Angular Momentum and Black Hole Mass Components of Sagittarius A*
comment: 6 pages, summary of oral report presented at the Galactic Center workshop 2026 (IAU Symposium 405, Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time)
summary: The dimensionless spin angular momentum, dimensionless spin function, and blackhole mass components of Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) were obtained by Daly et al. (2024) by applying the outflow method to six independent sets of simultaneously or contemporaneously obtained X-ray and radio data. Here, results obtained for Sgr A* with the outflow method are reviewed. Consistent results were obtained with each data set. Set I (the preferred data set) indicates that Sgr A* has a dimensionless spin angular momentum $a_* = (0.90 ~\pm~ 0.06)$ and a dimensionless spin function $F = (0.62 ~\pm~ 0.10)$. The results are consistent with the value of $a_* = (0.93~\pm~ 0.15)$ obtained with the outflow method applied to an independent data set (Daly 2019). The application of the outflow method to a weak compact radio source such as Sgr A* in its current state is most accurately determined with simultaneous or contemporaneous radio and X-ray measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews results from the outflow method applied to Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) using six independent X-ray and radio datasets. The preferred dataset yields a dimensionless spin angular momentum a* = 0.90 ± 0.06 and a dimensionless spin function F = 0.62 ± 0.10, consistent with prior independent measurements (a* = 0.93 ± 0.15, Daly 2019). The study emphasizes that contemporaneous radio and X-ray observations are essential for accurate spin determinations of weak compact radio sources like Sgr A*.
AI.motivation: To review and validate the outflow method results for determining the spin parameters and black hole mass components of Sagittarius A*, building on prior work by Daly et al. (2024) and comparing with independent measurements.
AI.method: The outflow method is applied to six independent sets of simultaneously or contemporaneously obtained X-ray and radio observations of Sgr A* to derive the dimensionless spin angular momentum, dimensionless spin function, and black hole mass components.
AI.result: Consistent results were obtained across all six datasets. The preferred dataset (Set I) gives a dimensionless spin angular momentum a* = 0.90 ± 0.06 and dimensionless spin function F = 0.62 ± 0.10, consistent with the independent measurement of a* = 0.93 ± 0.15 (Daly 2019).
AI.conclusion: The outflow method provides consistent and reliable spin estimates for Sgr A* across multiple datasets, and simultaneous or contemporaneous radio and X-ray measurements are crucial for accurately applying this method to weak compact radio sources in their current state.
